enquiry: We handle a petroleum stream and currently send samples to a laboratory for water determination. We want to investigate a fiber based measurement closer to the process so that changes can be noticed sooner. The analyzer would be outside the process area. Before selecting equipment, we need to know what to clarify and what a first comparison experiment should establish.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today when water changes in the stream are only known from laboratory results, and what decision should real-time data drive?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the value of earlier detection and which control action or alarm the measurement must support.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Earlier detection is assumed to support process monitoring; the specific decision is unknown and must be defined before equipment selection.

clarification_questions.question: What is the target water level in the petroleum stream, stated in ppm or %, and what range of values occurs?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the method needs trace or bulk sensitivity and whether a lab screening must focus on low or high concentrations.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening establishes whether the water content is at ppm or % level.

clarification_questions.question: What is the physical state and appearance of the stream at the sampling point (clear, turbid or opaque liquid, emulsion, or contains solids or gas)?
clarification_questions.why: Determines the probe geometry and whether transmission, reflection or ATR is suitable.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Sample appearance unknown; lab screening on representative samples establishes the optical properties before a probe is chosen.

clarification_questions.question: What are the process temperature, pressure and fouling risk at the measuring point, and how much does the stream composition vary over time?
clarification_questions.why: Affects probe material, fouling management, temperature compensation and the robustness of any calibration.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Process conditions unknown; the in-line trial must document temperature, pressure and fouling before scale-up.

clarification_questions.question: How far is the proposed analyzer from the measuring point, and are any optical fibers already installed between them?
clarification_questions.why: Determines the fiber type and whether mid-infrared transmission is feasible, since silica fibers cannot carry mid-IR.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Distance and existing fibers unknown; fiber type stays open until the link length and installed fibers are known.

clarification_questions.question: Which laboratory method is used for water determination today, what is its accuracy and repeatability, and how often are samples taken?
clarification_questions.why: The laboratory method is the reference for the comparison experiment and sets the accuracy the fiber method must match.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method and accuracy unknown; the comparison design cannot be fixed until the reference method is identified.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required for the fiber-based measurement?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the acceptance criteria for the first experiment and rules out options that cannot meet them.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the first experiment establishes achievable performance and the requirements are set afterwards.

flags_before_revision.detail: overstated: The claim says 'Mid-IR needs CIR or PIR fibers'. S02 p.6 lists chalcogenide As-S (1100-6500 nm), polycrystalline (3000 nm-17 um), hollow glass waveguides (2000 nm-18 um), and indium and zirconium fluoride fibers (up to 5500 and 4500 nm), all of which reach the mid-IR. CIR is also not named on the page. 'Needs' is stronger than the page supports. Fix: Replace 'Mid-IR needs CIR or PIR fibers' with 'S02 p.6 lists several fiber types that cover mid-IR (chalcogenide, polycrystalline, hollow glass waveguide, fluoride); silica fibers are not listed in that range.'

overstated: The claim says 'Mid-IR needs CIR or PIR fibers, not silica'. S02 p.6 shows that other mid-IR-capable fibers (chalcogenide, hollow glass waveguide, fluoride) also exist, and CIR is not named on the page. Fix: Rephrase to: 'S02 p.6 shows that silica fibers do not cover the mid-IR range and that mid-IR-capable fibers (for example polycrystalline or chalcogenide) must be confirmed for the remote link.'

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR fiber probes, their use in online analysis, and NIR overlapping bands that call for chemometrics. It says nothing about petroleum composition changes or water calibration becoming invalid. Fix: Cite S01 p.10 only for the general need for chemometric calibration of overlapping bands, or find an AFS source page that discusses calibration drift and state the risk as a general possibility.

not_supported: The cited table rows and S01 p.6 give an ATR optical depth of 1-6 um for IR, but none of them discuss deposits on the crystal or distorted readings. The deposit effect is an inference that the cited pages do not state. Fix: Keep the depth statement with citation to S01 p.6 (IR ATR depth 1-6 um) and S01 p.16 (evanescent wave penetrates a few micrometres), and mark the deposit effect as a general consideration rather than something the sources show.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [guidance]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [guidance]
